why_relevant: Mainstream daily with sustained coverage of the bank levy debate across political parties, including opinion/analysis pieces that map the political positions behind regulatory change.
Investigative daily; its rolling economics feed timestamps regulatory and levy developments as they break in parliament, useful for reconstructing deadline slippage.

Long-running aggregator of Slovak economic/banking newswire copy (TASR/SITA plus own desk); archives and re-publishes items that later disappear behind paywalls or from originating sites. Good snowball surface for actor names and product/regulatory events.

Public news agency TASR's free portal; carries verbatim ministry/NBS/parliament statements on banking legislation. Wire copy is the upstream of most Slovak banking-regulation stories, so it gives earliest timestamps.
Second Slovak news agency; tag pages per bank/institution act as a ready-made actor-indexed archive of regulatory and licensing events.
Sector-specific consumer/banking portal maintaining a bank register plus news; useful for tracking market entries/exits, licence changes and product-level effects of regulation.

News television with online economics desk; covers payments-infrastructure changes (instant payments, verification of payee) and regulatory go-live dates in accessible terms, plus on-record interviews with regulators/ministers.
Commercial broadcaster's portal; reported the parliamentary passage of the doubled bank levy and its pass-through to clients — the political-process layer around regulatory change.

EU-affairs outlet publishing in Slovak; the key bridge source explaining how EU financial-services files (CRR/CRD, PSD3/PSR, MiCA, instant payments) land in Slovak transposition, including consultation and deadline framing.

English-language Slovak outlet (SME stable); translates domestic banking/payments regulatory developments for an international audience — bridges the sk/en gap for cross-country comparison and gives durable English phrasing of local actor names.
Slovak crypto/fintech trade outlet; tracks MiCA licensing of Slovak CASPs, NBS authorisation decisions and payment-innovation rollouts (e.g. QR payments) that mainstream press under-reports.

Legal-professional media/portal carrying law-firm bylined commentary on amendments to the Banking Act and payment-services law; often the first substantive interpretation of a novela's practical obligations and effective dates.
Legal news portal with a topic hub for amendments (novela); tracks legislative pipeline items including financial-sector laws, giving early notice of consultation and effectiveness dates.

Commercial legal-information publisher indexing every Zbierka zákonov item with consolidated wording and commentary; its per-amendment pages (e.g. 30/2026 Z. z. novela zákona o bankách) are a precise pointer from a media mention to the exact legal instrument.

source_name: INESS – Institute of Economic and Social Studies
why_relevant: Think tank whose commentary is heavily syndicated by Slovak media; quantifies the bank levy burden and consolidation packages, providing the analytical frame journalists reuse. Acts as a semi-media amplifier for regulatory critique.

source_name: European Payments Council – news & insights (Slovakia items)
why_relevant: EU-level scheme body newsletter that periodically publishes country insight pieces on Slovak instant-payments adoption written by Slovak bank/SBA practitioners — an EU newsletter with genuine SK coverage.
Smaller Slovak personal-finance/news site with a financial-news tag stream; low authority but occasionally surfaces niche regulatory/product items. Value is breadth of the long tail, not reliability.

source_name: Profesia.sk — banking/compliance job listings (SK's dominant job board)
why_relevant: Profesia is the default hiring channel for every SK bank and most PSPs. Job titles and requirement bullets name specific regulations (DORA, PSD2/PSD3, AML/AMLR, CRR3, IFRS, FINREP/COREP, MiCA) months before implementation programmes surface publicly. Employer-filtered views (e.g. company_id) let you track a single bank's regulatory hiring wave over time.

Largest SK bank (Erste group). Its own postings carry richer role descriptions than aggregator copies and reveal named programme teams (e.g. regulatory reporting, ICT risk/DORA, AML transformation), which are proxies for internal implementation roadmaps.

source_name: Tatra banka careers (prirodzenenajlepsi.sk — Tatra banka / Raiffeisen SK employer site)
why_relevant: Tatra banka (RBI group) runs its recruitment on a dedicated employer-brand domain rather than the main bank site. Regulatory/compliance vacancies there indicate group-driven implementation programmes landing in SK.
Secondary SK job board that carries bank and financial-institution compliance roles not always mirrored on Profesia; useful as a cross-check and for smaller PSPs/e-money firms.

source_name: Jooble SK — aggregated compliance officer vacancies
why_relevant: Aggregator that surfaces postings from employer sites, agencies and niche boards in one place — good for discovering which employers (incl. non-bank PSPs, fintechs, shared-service centres) are hiring regulatory staff, then snowballing to the primary posting.
Additional SK aggregator with a wide employer index; useful for counting the volume of compliance/regulatory hiring over time as a crude intensity signal.

source_name: LinkedIn — Slovak bank company job pages (e.g. Slovenská sporiteľňa)
why_relevant: SK banks post senior/programme roles (DORA programme manager, regulatory reporting lead, AMLA readiness) in English on LinkedIn that never appear on SK boards. Also surfaces employee title changes that mark a new regulatory function being stood up.

Banks frequently outsource confidential regulatory-programme hiring to agencies; agency ads describe the workstream (e.g. 'reporting to NBS', 'DORA remediation') while masking the client, which is itself a signal that an unannounced programme exists.

The regulator's own event calendar is a leading indicator: a workshop announced for a regulation signals that supervisory expectations and reporting templates are imminent. Confirmed example found: a DORA workshop on the first level-2 package.

source_name: NBS conference series 'Slovenský finančný trh a inovácie' (annual)
why_relevant: NBS's flagship innovation/supervision conference; opened by the vice-governor and used to telegraph supervisory priorities (crypto-assets/MiCA, AI, open finance) ahead of formal guidance. Agendas and recordings are published.

source_name: NBS Governor — interviews and presentations page (rozhovory a prezentácie)
why_relevant: Central archive of governor Peter Kažimír's speeches, media contributions and conference presentations. Speeches routinely flag supervisory priorities and legislative timing before official consultation documents appear.

source_name: Inštitút bankového vzdelávania NBS, n.o. (IBV NBS) — course catalogue & conferences
why_relevant: The training arm founded by NBS (~120 courses on banking regulation, payments, accounting). New course titles are one of the earliest public traces of a regulation entering the SK market, because courses are built when banks start asking. Also runs the FinNext AML & Compliance conference.
